core.title: Machine Learning-assisted Antenna Design and Optimization: A Comprehensive Review of Surrogate Modeling, Active Learning, and Intelligent Optimization
core.abstract: The rapid development of wireless communication systems has created an increasing demand for compact, broadband, high-performance, and application-specific antennas. Conventional antenna design approaches generally rely on analytical formulations, empirical relationships, parameter sweeps, and repeated full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, which become computationally expensive as the number of design variables increases. To address these challenges, metaheuristic optimisation techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) have been widely investigated for exploring complex antenna design spaces. More recently, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches have been introduced for antenna performance prediction, inverse design, and surrogate-assisted optimisation. These approaches can reduce the computational burden associated with repeated EM simulations; however, their effectiveness often depends on sufficiently large and representative simulation datasets. Hybrid ML–metaheuristic approaches further improve the optimisation process by combining predictive models with intelligent search algorithms, while Active Learning enables the selective acquisition of informative simulation samples. This review presents the evolution of computational antenna design from conventional and metaheuristic approaches to ML-based, hybrid, and Active Learning-driven methodologies. The reviewed studies are critically examined with respect to their design strategies, optimisation techniques, simulation requirements, data dependence, and computational efficiency. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of surrogate modelling and adaptive sample selection in reducing expensive full-wave simulations. The review identifies the limitations of existing approaches and highlights the need for autonomous, data-efficient, and simulation-efficient frameworks for high-dimensional microstrip antenna optimisation.

extended.title: Fatigue characterization of hybrid fibre-reinforced concrete: S-N curve development, Weibull reliability modelling, and effect of variable amplitude loading
extended.abstract: Fatigue loading is a primary factor governing the durability and service life of structural concrete, necessitating materials with enhanced resistance to cyclic degradation. This study presents a detailed fatigue characterization of concrete prisms incorporating mono and hybrid fibre reinforcements under constant and variable amplitude flexural loading. Seven mixtures were investigated: normal concrete (NC), steel fibre -reinforced concrete (SFRC) at 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% volume fractions, and hybrid steel-polypropylene fibre-reinforced concrete (SF-PPF: 75: 25) in each volume fraction. Fatigue stress levels were decided based static flexural tests. Constant-amplitude fatigue tests were conducted at stress levels of 0.6–0.9 (stress ratio 0.1; 5 Hz), to construct S-N curve. It was observed from the extensive experiments that the synergetic effect of fibre reinforcement significantly improved fatigue performance by enhancing crack-bridging capacity, delaying crack propagation, and improving stiffness retention. Fatigue life decreased with increasing stress levels across all mixes; however, hybrid composites, exhibited substantially extended fatigue life. The S-N relationship was effectively described using the Basquin model, demonstrating strong agreement with experimental results. Probabilistic fatigue behaviour was evaluated using a two-parameter Weibull distribution, indicating reduced scatter and improved reliability for fibre-reinforced concretes compared to NC. Among all mixtures, the 1.5% hybrid fibre mix exhibited the highest fatigue life and improved damage resistance under cyclic loading conditions, whereas the 1.0% hybrid mix demonstrated comparatively lower fatigue-life scatter and better statistical reliability based on Weibull analysis. Overall, the optimal comprehensive performance was achieved through a balanced combination of fatigue durability and reliability characteristics.

papers.title: Machine Learning-assisted Antenna Design and Optimization: A Comprehensive Review of Surrogate Modeling, Active Learning, and Intelligent Optimization
papers.abstract: The rapid development of wireless communication systems has created an increasing demand for compact, broadband, high-performance, and application-specific antennas. Conventional antenna design approaches generally rely on analytical formulations, empirical relationships, parameter sweeps, and repeated full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations, which become computationally expensive as the number of design variables increases. To address these challenges, metaheuristic optimisation techniques such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimisation (PSO) have been widely investigated for exploring complex antenna design spaces. More recently, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) approaches have been introduced for antenna performance prediction, inverse design, and surrogate-assisted optimisation. These approaches can reduce the computational burden associated with repeated EM simulations; however, their effectiveness often depends on sufficiently large and representative simulation datasets. Hybrid ML–metaheuristic approaches further improve the optimisation process by combining predictive models with intelligent search algorithms, while Active Learning enables the selective acquisition of informative simulation samples. This review presents the evolution of computational antenna design from conventional and metaheuristic approaches to ML-based, hybrid, and Active Learning-driven methodologies. The reviewed studies are critically examined with respect to their design strategies, optimisation techniques, simulation requirements, data dependence, and computational efficiency. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of surrogate modelling and adaptive sample selection in reducing expensive full-wave simulations. The review identifies the limitations of existing approaches and highlights the need for autonomous, data-efficient, and simulation-efficient frameworks for high-dimensional microstrip antenna optimisation.

papers.title: Fatigue characterization of hybrid fibre-reinforced concrete: S-N curve development, Weibull reliability modelling, and effect of variable amplitude loading
papers.abstract: Fatigue loading is a primary factor governing the durability and service life of structural concrete, necessitating materials with enhanced resistance to cyclic degradation. This study presents a detailed fatigue characterization of concrete prisms incorporating mono and hybrid fibre reinforcements under constant and variable amplitude flexural loading. Seven mixtures were investigated: normal concrete (NC), steel fibre -reinforced concrete (SFRC) at 0.5%, 1.0%, and 1.5% volume fractions, and hybrid steel-polypropylene fibre-reinforced concrete (SF-PPF: 75: 25) in each volume fraction. Fatigue stress levels were decided based static flexural tests. Constant-amplitude fatigue tests were conducted at stress levels of 0.6–0.9 (stress ratio 0.1; 5 Hz), to construct S-N curve. It was observed from the extensive experiments that the synergetic effect of fibre reinforcement significantly improved fatigue performance by enhancing crack-bridging capacity, delaying crack propagation, and improving stiffness retention. Fatigue life decreased with increasing stress levels across all mixes; however, hybrid composites, exhibited substantially extended fatigue life. The S-N relationship was effectively described using the Basquin model, demonstrating strong agreement with experimental results. Probabilistic fatigue behaviour was evaluated using a two-parameter Weibull distribution, indicating reduced scatter and improved reliability for fibre-reinforced concretes compared to NC. Among all mixtures, the 1.5% hybrid fibre mix exhibited the highest fatigue life and improved damage resistance under cyclic loading conditions, whereas the 1.0% hybrid mix demonstrated comparatively lower fatigue-life scatter and better statistical reliability based on Weibull analysis. Overall, the optimal comprehensive performance was achieved through a balanced combination of fatigue durability and reliability characteristics.
